title: Construction & Precast Concrete
painPoint: Precast concrete producers rely on embedded NdFeB formwork magnets to clamp steel and aluminium shuttering, yet standard N42 blocks lose holding force after repeated steam-curing cycles at 60–80°C, where low-coercivity structures suffer gradual, irreversible demagnetization. Cement slurry, release agents and alkaline wash water attack unprotected nickel plating, causing corrosion and magnet loss inside expensive moulds. Lateral pressure from fresh concrete can shift weakly potted magnets, producing dimensional errors on architectural panels and tunnel segments. Procurement teams also struggle with inconsistent holding force between batches, forcing conservative magnet counts, heavier formwork and slower stripping cycles.
youjiuSolution: YOUJIU engineers potted formwork magnets around 42SH and 35UH sintered NdFeB cores, retaining coercivity through repeated 80°C steam cycles and delivering rated holding force from 450 kg to 900 kg with a 3:1 safety factor. Each assembly is sealed in a 304 stainless steel housing with epoxy encapsulation, surviving alkaline slurry and 500-hour salt spray without corrosion. Precision machined bases hold ±0.5 mm placement tolerance, while dual-pole designs resist lateral pressure from fresh concrete. We validate every batch on a pull-force test rig and can match your shuttering drawing; send it to our team for a priced proposal within 24 hours.
